newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: PLO's U.N. envoy condemns Jerusalem bombing.
newsitem.headline: PLO's U.N. envoy condemns Jerusalem bombing.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer condemned Wednesday's bombing of a market in West Jerusalem and said he did not see how any Palestinian could think such "criminal actions" would help the Palestinian cause.
It was also not the time to try to "score political points," Nasser al-Kidwa told reporters, alluding to calls by Israel for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to crack down on extremists.

"We do hope that the parties concerned will be able to overcome the situation quickly and proceed with the peace process as it was planned," he said, referring to an attack in which two Arab suicide bombers killed 13 other people and wounded more than 150.

"The Palestinian side at all levels has condemned the bombings which took place today in West Jerusalem. We have established policy in this regard opposing any actions committed against innocent civilians from both sides," al-Kidwa said.
"And frankly, as a Palestinian, I do not see how could any Palestinian see any benefit to the Palestinian people coming out of such criminal actions."

Asked about a statement by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that expressions of regret were not adequate and that action was needed, al-Kidwa said: "I believe that we have done all what we could do. We believe that we have lived up to our commitment."

It was "not time to try to score points, especially political points," he added. "Because if we try, then both sides will start accusing the other for being responsible for many things, including creating a certain atmosphere, making life miserable for the Palestinian people, etc etc."
Asked whether Arafat could control extremist Palestinian factions, al-Kidwa said: "We can do our best but we cannot guarantee 100 percent results. We don't think that anyone else could."

Questioned whether the bombing had set back the Middle East peace process, he said: "The peace process was in very bad shape anyway. It might have further endangered it. But if we are serious we have to look for serious solutions ... commitment to fulfil all our contractual obligations, both sides ... Finger-pointing and attempts to score points are things which should not be attempted at this stage."
